difference: Does a single on-screen object, action or cut stand in, in one stroke, for a real situation that is never itself shown (metaphor/metonymy/synecdoche), while the film's own drive is still action discovering situation?
axis: trope that converts one action-form into the other: [perfect trope in one moment, small form carried by large (eS(S))] → imperfect trope sustained over a sequence, large form carried by small (S→iA) → nesting so recursive you cannot tell which form contains which

confusions.name: Theatrical figure
confusions.flip: It is Theatrical instead if the figure is not a single substituted image but a staged fictitious action (a play, game, rehearsal, parody) that runs over a sequence and prefigures a real act the film keeps deferring.
confusions.why_not: A plastic figure is instantaneous and substitutive: the slaughtered bull replaces the massacre in one cut; nothing is rehearsed or deferred.

confusions.name: Symbol
confusions.flip: It is a Symbol instead if the object's meaning is an abstract relation that organises the whole plot (a key, a necklace binding characters in a Hitchcockian relation) rather than a figure for a situation kept in ellipsis.
confusions.why_not: The plastic figure points past itself to a real situation the film does not show; the symbol is a concrete object carrying a relation the film does show being exchanged.

confusions.name: Index of lack
confusions.flip: It is an Index of lack instead if the shown action is literal and simply lets us infer an unshown situation (an elision in the chain of events), with no figural substitution.
confusions.why_not: The index of lack is inference from a gap; the plastic figure is a trope: the shown thing means something other than itself.

counterfeit: An insert of a ticking clock during a wait looks like a plastic figure but is only a literal action-image detail (time pressure inside the situation), not a trope standing for an unshown situation.

confidence.high: A cut or insert substitutes an unrelated image for an event the film never shows directly, and the substitution is legible as metaphor/metonymy (Strike's bull for the workers).
confidence.medium: A recurring object that the film loads with meaning beyond its narrative use, but the implied situation is partly shown too.
confidence.low: Any 'meaningful' object whose significance is only interpretive and not built by editing or repetition.

deamer_anchor: "an object which has a meaning beyond itself" (p. 107)

difference: Is a fictitious action (performance, game, allegory, parody) being played out over a sequence as a precursor of a real action that has not yet happened and keeps being deferred?
axis: trope that converts one action-form into the other: perfect trope in one moment, small form carried by large (eS(S)) → [imperfect trope sustained over a sequence, large form carried by small (S→iA)] → nesting so recursive you cannot tell which form contains which

confusions.name: Plastic figure
confusions.flip: It is Plastic instead if the figure collapses into one substituted image or cut rather than a sustained performed sequence.
confusions.why_not: The theatrical figure is linear and repeated; it needs duration and at least one repetition to prefigure.

confusions.name: Mise en abyme
confusions.flip: It is Mise en abyme instead if the performance contains figures that in turn contain the performance, so we cannot tell which level is the real action and which the rehearsal.
confusions.why_not: In a theatrical figure the real/fictitious hierarchy holds: the play prefigures, the real act eventually arrives (or is known to be the thing deferred).

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is Powers of the false instead if there is no real action the performance prefigures at all: every level is equally a forgery and truth is no longer the horizon.
confusions.why_not: The theatrical figure is still a movement-image trope: it depends on a real action to come.

counterfeit: A scene of actors on a stage in a backstage musical looks theatrical, but if the show is just the narrative's own situation (putting on a show) it is plain action-image, not a figure prefiguring some other real action.

confidence.high: A staged fiction is repeated and its structure visibly maps onto a real confrontation that follows (To Be or Not to Be's performance becoming the escape).
confidence.medium: An allegorical sequence whose correspondence to the real action is clear but unrepeated.
confidence.low: A single shot of a performance: whether it prefigures anything cannot be seen in the shot.

deamer_anchor: "a sequence of images as precursor of the real action" (p. 107)

difference: Do figures nest inside figures such that, watching, you cannot say whether a performed sequence contains an emblematic image or an emblematic image contains the performed sequence?
axis: trope that converts one action-form into the other: perfect trope in one moment, small form carried by large (eS(S)) → imperfect trope sustained over a sequence, large form carried by small (S→iA) → [nesting so recursive you cannot tell which form contains which]

confusions.name: Theatrical figure
confusions.flip: It is Theatrical instead if the nested performance has a clear outside: one real action that the play-within points toward.
confusions.why_not: Mise en abyme loses the outside; the recursion is the point.

confusions.name: Mirrors face to face
confusions.flip: It is Mirrors face to face instead if the recursion is optical, actual and virtual images exchanging in literal reflective surfaces with no trope or narrative prefiguring at stake.
confusions.why_not: Mise en abyme is a recursion of figures (tropes of action and situation); the crystal is a recursion of the actual/virtual image itself, time-image not action.

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is Powers of the false instead if the nested levels are incompossible versions with no true one and the characters are forgers of time.
confusions.why_not: Mise en abyme still converts action-forms; it disorients reflection but does not abolish the true.

counterfeit: A shot of a TV playing the same film we are watching looks like mise en abyme, but if it is a one-off gag that does not fold the film's small and large forms into one another it is only a visual quip.

confidence.high: A film where the frame-within repeatedly becomes the frame (Source Code's loop in a replica cockpit) and the viewer loses which level is originary.
confidence.medium: A strong image-within-image that recurs but whose top level stays secure.
confidence.low: A single frame-within-frame composition; visual nesting alone is not the sign.

deamer_anchor: "It is as if we enter and become lost in a hall of mirrors" (p. 108) - Deamer's naming

difference: Does the character's action visibly exceed anything the situation requires, so that the grandiose act makes the situation look futile (a steamship hauled over a mountain)?
axis: where the disproportion between action and situation lies: [action outsizes a futile situation (sAs)] → futile action reveals an immense situation (aSa) → sAs = aSa, trivial and immense indistinguishable

confusions.name: Figure of enfeeblement
confusions.flip: It is Enfeeblement instead if the character is small, aimless and ineffective and it is the world that swells up around them.
confusions.why_not: In the sublime the character is the outsized force; the world shrinks to a futile encompasser.

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is Milieu instead if the situation determines and justifies the heroic response, a large-form SAS where action answers the milieu and modifies it.
confusions.why_not: The sublime action is not required by the situation; the ratio between act and givens is broken.

confusions.name: Imprint
confusions.flip: It is an Imprint instead if the excess is interior and explained: a psychological obsession or buried drive drives the act and the film reads it as character causality.
confusions.why_not: The sublime is hallucinatory and visionary; the act exposes the situation as absurd rather than exposing the character's hidden motive.

counterfeit: An action hero single-handedly storming a fortress looks sublime, but if the plot's threat really does require the feat it is large-form action (SAS), not an inverted sAs.

confidence.high: The enterprise is visibly absurd relative to its goal and the film stages it as hypnotic or visionary (Aguirre, Fitzcarraldo, Four Lions' plan).
confidence.medium: Over-reaction is clear but the film partly endorses it as justified.
confidence.low: A single spectacular gesture without knowledge of what the situation demanded.

deamer_anchor: "the behaviours of the character overwhelm the givens of the situation" (p. 111)

difference: Do a weak character's small, futile acts make an immense, indifferent world swell into view (the tiny point fleeing to the horizon), rather than the world merely sitting there?
axis: where the disproportion between action and situation lies: action outsizes a futile situation (sAs) → [futile action reveals an immense situation (aSa)] → sAs = aSa, trivial and immense indistinguishable

confusions.name: Quotidian
confusions.flip: It is Quotidian instead if the small acts are neither futile nor merely revelatory but carry their own petty heroism, so trivial and immense can't be separated.
confusions.why_not: Enfeeblement keeps the inversion one-way: the act is futile, the world is sublime.

confusions.name: Opsign
confusions.flip: It is an Opsign instead if the character no longer acts at all (a seer, not a weakling doing something) and the situation is a pure optical one cut from any sensory-motor response.
confusions.why_not: The enfeebled still acts, however feebly; the small form is inverted, not broken.

confusions.name: Any-space-whatever
confusions.flip: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the vast space is emptied or disconnected and carries affect in itself, with no character action measuring it.
confusions.why_not: Enfeeblement needs the weakling's act as the measure that reveals the grandiose; remove the act and it becomes affection.

counterfeit: An establishing extreme long shot of a hiker on a ridge looks like enfeeblement but is just a perception/milieu shot unless the character's acts across the film are shown as futile against that world.

confidence.high: Recurrent futile, aimless acts by idiot/weakling figures staged against indifferent vastness (Stroszek, Kaspar Hauser).
confidence.medium: A slacker or drifter film where weakness is clear but the world is not made to swell.

deamer_anchor: "weak characters reveal the sublime nature of the world" (p. 112)

difference: Is an everyday act shown so that you cannot decide whether it is trivial or heroic, the situation both inconsequential and unfathomable at once?
axis: where the disproportion between action and situation lies: action outsizes a futile situation (sAs) → futile action reveals an immense situation (aSa) → [sAs = aSa, trivial and immense indistinguishable]

confusions.name: Figure of enfeeblement
confusions.flip: It is Enfeeblement instead if the act reads plainly as futile and the world plainly as overwhelming.
confusions.why_not: In the quotidian the petty function is itself the heroism; neither pole dominates.

confusions.name: Opsign
confusions.flip: It is an Opsign instead if the everyday is shown as a pure optical situation where no one can act at all (Ozu's empty vase, still lifes) rather than as an act of duty.
confusions.why_not: The quotidian is still an action-figure: the character works, serves, carries on.

confusions.name: Body of attitude
confusions.flip: It is Body of attitude instead if the everyday is carried by the tired, waiting body whose postures express time, and action has dropped out.
confusions.why_not: The quotidian is about the ambivalent value of action, not the body's time.

counterfeit: A montage of morning routines (coffee, commute) looks quotidian but is merely exposition unless the film makes the routine simultaneously petty and weighty.

confidence.high: Across a film, a duty-bound ordinary job is shown both as servility and as the only ground of valour (A Screaming Man).
confidence.medium: Everyday life is foregrounded but tilts clearly toward either sublime or futile.
confidence.low: Any single domestic or workplace shot.

deamer_anchor: "the pettiness of our function is the heroism of life" (p. 113) - Deamer's naming

difference: Before acting, does the character have to extract a question hidden in the situation (what is a samurai now?), so action is delayed into a considered response rather than an explosive reaction?
axis: where the problem is located: [a priori, hidden in the situation and extracted before a considered act] → a posteriori, actions assemble heterogeneous pieces that stay a cipher → everywhere, no originary form, the world itself a field of problems

confusions.name: Limit of the small form
confusions.flip: It is the Small-form limit instead if there is no given situation holding a question; the question is assembled from heterogeneous actions and stays unanswered.
confusions.why_not: In Ll the milieu is given and the question is a priori; a response is eventually possible.

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is Milieu instead if the situation simply provokes the character to a direct reply (SAS) with no pause to formulate its question.
confusions.why_not: Ll suspends the duel/response in favour of investigating the situation's givens.

confusions.name: Extreme limit
confusions.flip: It is the Extreme limit instead if you can't tell whether the problem came from the situation or from the actions, and the whole world has become a cipher of forces.
confusions.why_not: Ll still has a determinate milieu and a direction toward answer.

counterfeit: A detective interrogating witnesses looks like a problem being extracted, but a whodunit's question is a missing fact, not a question hidden in the milieu that redefines what action can be.

confidence.high: The narrative visibly stalls action to investigate the givens and ends with an act framed as answer to the question (Seven Samurai, Ikiru).
confidence.medium: A questing structure where the question is posed but the response is conventional.
confidence.low: Any single shot; the sign is a narrative trajectory.

difference: Do parallel, heterogeneous lines of action connect only as pieces from different puzzles, so the situation they reveal remains an unanswered cipher, a sustained ellipsis?
axis: where the problem is located: a priori, hidden in the situation and extracted before a considered act → [a posteriori, actions assemble heterogeneous pieces that stay a cipher] → everywhere, no originary form, the world itself a field of problems

confusions.name: Limit of the large form
confusions.flip: It is the Large-form limit instead if a single given milieu poses the question and a considered response closes it.
confusions.why_not: Ls has no originating situation; action cannot disclose one.

confusions.name: Index of equivocity
confusions.flip: It is an Index of equivocity instead if a single action points ambiguously to two possible situations and the film eventually decides between them.
confusions.why_not: Equivocity is a doubled reading of one situation; Ls is many incongruent lines whose sum is a question.

confusions.name: Forking paths
confusions.flip: It is Forking paths instead if the heterogeneous lines are memories, flashbacks within flashbacks that never reconcile.
confusions.why_not: Ls is a present-tense action structure, not a structure of recollection.

counterfeit: An ensemble hyperlink film cutting between strangers looks like special homogeneity, but if the lines converge on a revealed answer (the crash, the twist) it is small-form action, not its limit.

confidence.high: Several distinct lines of action (often through women's lives in Mizoguchi) are kept heterogeneous and the film refuses the connecting answer.
confidence.medium: Multi-strand structure with only partial closure.

deamer_anchor: "all the pieces belong to different puzzles" (p. 117)

difference: Is the film permeated by problems from start to end so that you can no longer tell whether they are posed by the situation or discovered by action, the world itself appearing as a field of indeterminate forces?
axis: where the problem is located: a priori, hidden in the situation and extracted before a considered act → a posteriori, actions assemble heterogeneous pieces that stay a cipher → [everywhere, no originary form, the world itself a field of problems]

confusions.name: Limit of the small form
confusions.flip: It is the Small-form limit instead if the question is still traceable to the characters' actions building a cipher, with a clear action-to-situation direction.
confusions.why_not: Xl collapses the direction; the originary form is undecidable.

confusions.name: Any-space-whatever
confusions.flip: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the space is encountered as pure affect (quality/power) with no problem being worked through by action or thought.
confusions.why_not: Xl is the return to the any-space-whatever inside thought: action is still interrogating, now ungrounded.

confusions.name: Opsign
confusions.flip: It is an Opsign instead if action has actually broken down and characters only see and hear.
confusions.why_not: Xl is the limit of action-images still within the movement-image; the characters still pursue a problem.

counterfeit: A sci-fi film full of enigmas (a mysterious monolith) looks like a world of problems, but if the enigma is a plot device eventually explained it is ordinary action suspense.

confidence.high: Across a whole film, situation and action both become questions and the landscape reads as a cipher (Dersu Uzala's taiga, Monsters' infected zone).
confidence.medium: Pervasive enigma with residual originary direction.
confidence.low: Single shots of a hostile, enigmatic space - indistinguishable from As.

deamer_anchor: "A whole world of problems, puzzles, questions and ciphers." (p. 118) - Deamer's naming

difference: Is the passage into the dream explicitly marked and ornately made (dissolves, superimpositions, effects), with an equally marked exit, so the dream is attributed to a dreamer and recognised as dream by the viewer?
axis: dream marking: [explicit, ornate entry and exit] → invisible entry, ambiguous, uncanny-but-concrete → none, the world itself dreams and includes the dreamer

confusions.name: Restrained dream
confusions.flip: It is Restrained instead if entry is a straight cut and the dream looks like concrete everyday reality with only an uncanny slip.
confusions.why_not: The rich dream announces itself: 'This is a dream!'

confusions.name: Strong destiny
confusions.flip: It is Strong destiny instead if the marked dissolve leads not into an impossible world but into a realistic past event that then determines the character's action.
confusions.why_not: A rich dream's content is impossible and abstracting; a flashback's content is a past that happened.

confusions.name: Mirrors face to face
confusions.flip: It is Mirrors face to face instead if the superimposition/reflection doesn't lead into a dreamer's world but makes actual and virtual images endlessly exchange with no one dreaming.
confusions.why_not: The rich dream has a dreamer and a return; the crystal has no subject-anchored entry or exit.

counterfeit: A psychedelic music-video sequence of superimposed abstractions looks like a rich dream but lacks the dreamer-centred entry and exit, so it is formal abstraction (perhaps a gaseous perception), not a dream-image.

confidence.high: A character falls asleep, an ornate transition leads into impossible imagery, and a marked awakening returns (Sherlock Jr.).
confidence.medium: Overtly oneiric imagery with clear attribution but no marked return.
confidence.low: Heavily effected imagery without a visible dreamer.

deamer_anchor: "This is a dream! – such is the formula of the rich dream" (p. 123)

difference: Is the dream entered by an invisible cut and made of concrete everyday things with one impossible unhinging, so that the film's task becomes deciding whether we are awake?
axis: dream marking: explicit, ornate entry and exit → [invisible entry, ambiguous, uncanny-but-concrete] → none, the world itself dreams and includes the dreamer

confusions.name: Rich dream
confusions.flip: It is Rich instead if the entry is ornate and the imagery overtly strange.
confusions.why_not: The restrained dream hides its marking; you only learn it was a dream afterward, if ever.

confusions.name: Weak destiny
confusions.flip: It is Weak destiny instead if the unmarked intrusion turns out to be a past event (an incomplete memory) rather than an impossible present.
confusions.why_not: Restrained dream content is impossible or uncanny; weak-destiny content is a real past, just fragmentary.

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is Powers of the false instead if the ambiguity is never meant to be resolved and no dreamer anchors it: real and imaginary are undecidable in principle.
confusions.why_not: The restrained dream is still attributed to a dreamer and the film works to separate dream from real.

counterfeit: A shot that looks slightly 'off' (odd colour grade, eerie silence) seems like a restrained dream, but without a later revelation or impossibility it is mood, not a dream-image.

confidence.high: A film retrospectively reveals straight-cut sequences as dreams and makes that uncertainty its subject (Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie).
confidence.medium: One unmarked dream revealed by waking, without the film thematising the doubt.
confidence.low: Any single shot: by definition nothing in the shot marks it.

deamer_anchor: "Was I asleep? Am I now awake?" (p. 124)

difference: Is there no entry or exit at all: does the world itself carry the character along (song, dance, impossible events treated as natural) so that no one is the dreamer?
axis: dream marking: explicit, ornate entry and exit → invisible entry, ambiguous, uncanny-but-concrete → [none, the world itself dreams and includes the dreamer]

confusions.name: Rich dream
confusions.flip: It is Rich instead if the number or fantasy is framed as a character's reverie with a marked return to a non-musical reality.
confusions.why_not: In movement of world the fantasy is the reality; there is nothing outside it.

confusions.name: Body of gest
confusions.flip: It is Body of gest instead if the bodies' theatricalised ceremony or gesture creates the time and nothing requires a world-movement to supplant the character's action.
confusions.why_not: Movement of world is a movement-image: the world's movement takes over the character's faltering motor act.

confusions.name: Seed and environment
confusions.flip: It is Seed and environment instead if the enchanted world is a crystal that grows from a seed and is closed, time-crystallised (e.g. a stage world that the crystal contains) rather than a dream-circuit of anamorphoses.
confusions.why_not: Movement of world is still a mental-image of the dream, with a sensory-motor subject carried along.

counterfeit: A realist street scene with a busker singing looks like a musical number, but the world doesn't move the characters: song is diegetic performance, not movement of world.

confidence.high: A passerby's walk turns into dance, and the set, light and crowd move with it without any sleep frame (Singin' in the Rain title number, Band Wagon).
confidence.medium: Pervasive fantasy with vestiges of a framing reality.
confidence.low: A single dance shot without knowing whether it is framed.

deamer_anchor: "There is no entrance to the dream world, and no exit." (p. 125)

difference: Does a marked flashback (pause, dissolve, monochrome, reverb) return to the present and pass through affect into an action it determines, closing a causal circuit?
axis: how far the flashback travels into the present: [through affect into action (closed causal circuit)] → into affect only, a clue to be reconstructed → replaces perception, the past explored for itself

confusions.name: Weak destiny
confusions.flip: It is Weak destiny instead if the flashback is unmarked or incomplete and settles into the present's mood without yet driving an act.
confusions.why_not: Strong destiny's past is clear and it fuels a decisive act.

confusions.name: Rich dream
confusions.flip: It is a Rich dream instead if the marked transition opens onto impossible, transformed imagery rather than a realistic past.
confusions.why_not: Strong destiny's content is what happened.

confusions.name: Sheets of the past
confusions.flip: It is Sheets of the past instead if we move among coexisting regions of the past, none decisive, with no single recollection closing a circuit to action.
confusions.why_not: Strong destiny uses the past to explain; sheets explore the past as virtual coexistence.

counterfeit: A dissolve to a nostalgic childhood scene looks like strong destiny but is merely a memory-illustration if it doesn't determine any action in the present.

confidence.high: Marked flashback structure whose past explains a present fatal act (Le jour se lève, Double Indemnity).
confidence.medium: Marked flashback with affective payoff but loose causal link.

deamer_anchor: "allows the recollection to pass through the affect and into action" (p. 131)

difference: Is the flashback ambiguous, incomplete or shared, so it saturates present feeling as a clue to an ellipsis that must be reconstructed before any action can follow?
axis: how far the flashback travels into the present: through affect into action (closed causal circuit) → [into affect only, a clue to be reconstructed] → replaces perception, the past explored for itself

confusions.name: Strong destiny
confusions.flip: It is Strong destiny instead if the flashback is clearly marked and complete and directly produces an action.
confusions.why_not: Weak destiny stalls action; the past is a puzzle, not a cause.

confusions.name: Restrained dream
confusions.flip: It is a Restrained dream instead if the unmarked intrusion is impossible rather than a past event.
confusions.why_not: Weak destiny content is real past, fragmentary.

confusions.name: Sheets of the past
confusions.flip: It is Sheets of the past instead if no ellipsis is ultimately resolved and the film moves among coexisting ages of the past without a present to rescue.
confusions.why_not: Weak destiny still aims at reconstruction and resolution.

counterfeit: A non-linear edit that shuffles chronology for suspense looks like weak destiny, but if it isn't a character's memory saturating affect, it is simply narration order.

confidence.high: Fragmentary flashbacks from one or several characters are revisited and pieced together (White Material).
confidence.medium: Unmarked memory fragments that are eventually explained.
confidence.low: Single shot; cannot even establish that it is a memory.

deamer_anchor: "consents the recollection to pass into the affect" (p. 131)

difference: Do flashbacks fork within flashbacks, irreconcilably, so the past is explored for its own sake as an inexplicable secret and psychological causality is shown to be a ruse?
axis: how far the flashback travels into the present: through affect into action (closed causal circuit) → into affect only, a clue to be reconstructed → [replaces perception, the past explored for itself]

confusions.name: Weak destiny
confusions.flip: It is Weak destiny instead if the fragments eventually cohere and resolve the present ellipsis.
confusions.why_not: Forking paths never reconcile; the secret remains.

confusions.name: Sheets of the past
confusions.flip: It is Sheets of the past instead if the forking no longer passes through flashbacks at all but directly through coexistent regions of pure past, with no present anchoring the recollections.
confusions.why_not: Forking paths is still a movement-image of memory: actualised flashbacks returning to a present.

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is Powers of the false instead if the contradictory versions are not memories of a secret but forgeries that make truth itself undecidable.
confusions.why_not: Forking paths assumes a past that happened, just unreachable.

counterfeit: A multi-narrator courtroom film looks like forking paths, but if the versions are adjudicated and one truth emerges, it is weak destiny.

confidence.high: Nested multi-narrator flashbacks whose accounts do not reconcile (Mankiewicz).
confidence.medium: Nested flashbacks with only partial contradiction.

deamer_anchor: "the movie explores the past for itself" (p. 130)
